answer.label: Based on words by
answer.sourceLine: The thought comes from Locke’s Essay Concerning Human Understanding, Book I, chapter III, §3, in the inspected Gutenberg text. Locke actually begins, “I have always thought”; the compact sentence credited to Joyce is a grammatical recasting.

source.heading: The source

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Locke is answering an objection to his rejection of innate moral principles. People’s conduct, he argues, is evidence of what they believe, and actual conduct varies too much to establish the universal agreement his opponents need.

The line became a general maxim when extracted from that argument. Its modern introductory “The actions” and added verb should be identified as a recasting, while the underlying passage should be credited to Locke.
